_meta.indication: DAKLINZA is indicated for use with sofosbuvir for the treatment of patients with chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) genotype 3 infection; SVR rates are reduced in genotype 3 patients with cirrhosis treated for 12 weeks

pivotal_trials.trial_name: ALLY-3 (AI444218), a phase 3 study of daclatasvir plus sofosbuvir in HCV genotype 3
pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in the reviewed documents
pivotal_trials.design: Global, open-label, single-arm study with two cohorts (treatment-naive and treatment-experienced)
pivotal_trials.population: Treatment-naive or peginterferon/ribavirin treatment-experienced adults chronically infected with HCV genotype 3, with compensated liver disease
pivotal_trials.endpoint: SVR12, defined as HCV RNA < LLOQ (target detected or target not detected) at post-treatment Week 12
pivotal_trials.result: Overall SVR12 89% (135/152; 95% CI 83%, 93%); 90% (91/101) in treatment-naive and 86% (44/51) in treatment-experienced; SVR12 lower in cirrhotic (63%, 20/32) vs non-cirrhotic (96%, 115/120) subjects

nct_ctgov.title: Phase III Daclatasvir and Sofosbuvir for Genotype 3 Chronic HCV

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>=10%) with DAKLINZA plus sofosbuvir were headache (14%) and fatigue (14%); serious symptomatic bradycardia reported when coadministered with sofosbuvir and amiodarone
target_moa: Daclatasvir is an inhibitor of HCV nonstructural protein 5A (NS5A); it binds to the N-terminus of NS5A and inhibits both viral RNA replication and virion assembly

rems.type: There are currently no recommendations for Postmarket Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategies related to these NDA submissions

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee meeting was held for this application; the NDA was the third drug in the NS5A inhibitor class and raised no issues warranting discussion

description.text: Extended indication to HCV genotype 1, including HCV/HIV-1 co-infection, decompensated (Child-Pugh B/C) cirrhosis, and post-liver transplant patients, in combination with sofosbuvir ± ribavirin

citations.quote: Proposed Indication(s)	Chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) genotype (GT) 1, including HCV/HIV-1 co-infection and HCV decompensated cirrhosis and post-transplant population

description.text: Expanded indication to include genotype-1 chronic HCV patients co-infected with HIV-1, and added dosing for genotype-3 HCV/HIV-1 co-infected patients

citations.quote: This “Prior Approval” supplemental new drug application proposes to expand the indication to include the treatment of subjects with genotype-1 chronic hepatitis C virus infection, including subjects who are co-infected with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV-1) based on the results from the ALLY-2 clinical trial. In addition, dosage recommendations are added to include treatment of HCV genotype 3 subjects who are co-infected with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV-1). The labeling is also updated with drug-drug interaction information, including information for buprenorphine/naloxone and multiple HIV antiviral agents.

description.text: Expanded to include treatment of chronic HCV genotype 1 with compensated or decompensated cirrhosis and genotype 3 with decompensated cirrhosis

citations.quote: This “Prior Approval” supplemental new drug application proposes to expand the patient population to include the treatment of chronic hepatitis C virus genotype 1 infection in subjects with compensated (Child-Pugh A) or decompensated (Child-Pugh B or C) cirrhosis and treatment of chronic hepatitis C virus genotype 3 infection in subjects with decompensated (Child-Pugh B or C) cirrhosis.

basis.text: Breakthrough Therapy designation was granted to the DCV/asunaprevir (DUAL) combination for genotype 1b chronic HCV, not to the daclatasvir plus sofosbuvir genotype 3 regimen approved here

citations.quote: Breakthrough Therapy designation was granted to DCV/ASV (DUAL) combination therapy for the treatment of genotype 1b, chronic hepatitis C virus infection on 03-Feb-2014.

basis.text: Fast Track designation was granted to daclatasvir (DCV) on 08-Sep-2008

citations.quote: Fast Track designation was granted to DCV and ASV on 08-Sep-2008 and 31-Dec-2009, respectively.

summary.text: Daclatasvir (an HCV NS5A inhibitor) received Fast Track designation in 2008; the genotype 3 NDA for use with sofosbuvir was approved after an initial November 25, 2014 complete response letter, via a February 13, 2015 resubmission with no advisory committee meeting and traditional (non-accelerated) approval based on the ALLY-3 SVR12 results

citations.quote: Fast Track designation was granted to DCV and ASV on 08-Sep-2008 and 31-Dec-2009, respectively.
On November 25, 2014, the agency issued a complete response letter (CRL) for NDA 206,843. This resubmission is in response to the CRL.
No advisory committee meeting was held for this application.

requirement.text: 2930-1: Conduct a study to evaluate the pharmacokinetics, safety and treatment response (SVR) of daclatasvir in combination with other direct acting antivirals in pediatric subjects 3 through 17 years of age with chronic hepatitis C (deferred pediatric study under PREA)

citations.quote: 2930-1 Conduct a study to evaluate the pharmacokinetics, safety and treatment response (using sustained virologic response) of daclatasvir in combination with other direct acting antivirals in pediatric subjects 3 through 17 years of age with chronic hepatitis C.

requirement.text: 2930-2: Conduct an observational study to characterize the long-term (>=1 year) persistence of treatment-emergent daclatasvir resistance-associated substitutions in HCV genotype 3 infected subjects who failed daclatasvir-containing regimens

citations.quote: 2930-2 Conduct an observational study to characterize the long-term (\ge 1 year) persistence of treatment-emergent daclatasvir resistance-associated substitutions in hepatitis C virus genotype 3 infected subjects who failed treatment with daclatasvir-containing treatment regimens.

requirement.text: 2930-3: Evaluate the potential mechanism of pharmacodynamic and pharmacokinetic interactions between amiodarone and HCV direct acting antivirals, including daclatasvir, using a multielectrode array electrophysiology study in human stem-cell derived cardiomyocytes

citations.quote: 2930-3 Evaluate the potential mechanism of both pharmacodynamic and pharmacokinetic interactions between amiodarone and HCV direct acting antivirals, including daclatasvir, using a multielectrode array electrophysiology study in human stem-cell derived cardiomyocytes.

requirement.text: 2930-4: Evaluate the effect of individual HCV direct acting antivirals including daclatasvir on the plasma protein binding of amiodarone using the TRANSIL high sensitivity binding assay

citations.quote: 2930-4 Evaluate the effect of individual HCV direct acting antivirals including daclatasvir on the plasma protein binding of amiodarone using the TRANSIL® high sensitivity binding assay to help elucidate the potential mechanism of an interaction between amiodarone and HCV direct acting antivirals.

requirement.text: 2930-5: Conduct a trial in HCV genotype 3 infected subjects with cirrhosis treated with daclatasvir plus sofosbuvir to determine whether a longer treatment duration or addition of ribavirin reduces virologic failure and treatment-emergent drug resistance

citations.quote: 2930-5 Conduct a trial in hepatitis C virus genotype 3 infected subjects with cirrhosis treated with daclatasvir plus sofosbuvir to determine if a longer duration of treatment or the addition of ribavirin reduces the rate of virologic failure and the rate of treatment-emergent drug resistant viral populations.
